title: Autofluorescence imaging for human pluripotent stem cell differentiation into cardiomyocytes
protocol: Maintain human H9 embryonic stem cells on Matrigel-coated surfaces in mTeSR1.
Maintain human IMR90-4 induced pluripotent stem cells on Matrigel-coated surfaces in mTeSR1.
Maintain NKX2.5 EGFP/+ hPSCs on Matrigel-coated surfaces in mTeSR1.
Singularize hPSCs with Accutase.
Plate singularized hPSCs onto Matrigel-coated plates at a density ranging from 2.9 × 10^4 cells/cm² to 5.7 × 10^5 cells/cm².
Supplement mTeSR1 with 10 µM Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitor Y-27632 for two days before initiating differentiation.
Initiate differentiation by activating Wnt signaling with 8 µM to 12 µM CHIR99021 on day 0.
Inhibit Wnt signaling with 5 µM IPW2 on day 3.
Enable sequential excitation of NAD(P)H and FAD using an ultrafast tunable laser source.
Isolate NAD(P)H emission using a 440/80 nm bandpass filter.
Isolate FAD emission using a 550/100 nm bandpass filter.
Acquire fluorescence lifetime decays with 256 time bins across 256 × 256 pixel images.
Set the laser power at the sample to approximately 2.3 mW for NAD(P)H excitation and 7.9 mW for FAD excitation.
Perform imaging through a 40×/1.15 NA objective (Nikon).
Conduct FLIM on differentiation day 0, day 1, day 3, and day 5.
Collect day 8 NAD(P)H lifetime variables for NKX2.5<sup>EGFP/+</sup> hPSCs.
Perform two-photon excitation of NKX2.5-EGFP at 890 nm.
Use a 500LP dichroic mirror during imaging.
Collect images from H9 embryonic stem cells before and after 10 mM 2DG treatment for the 2DG experiment.
Collect images from H9 embryonic stem cells before and after 10 μM rotenone treatment for the rotenone experiment.
